steps.title: Compare the two prices on each row
steps.change: The comparison can be true, false, or unknown. Products is the only source because Sale_Price and Market_Price sit on each product row, so the full-price comparison needs no join.
steps.added_sql:
SELECT ProductID, Product, Sale_Price, Market_Price,
       Market_Price = Sale_Price AS prices_match
FROM Products
ORDER BY ProductID;
steps.sql:
SELECT ProductID, Product, Sale_Price, Market_Price,
       Market_Price = Sale_Price AS prices_match
FROM Products
ORDER BY ProductID;

steps.title: Keep products with equal prices
steps.added_sql:
SELECT ProductID, Product, Brand, Sale_Price, Market_Price
-- …
WHERE Market_Price = Sale_Price
steps.sql:
SELECT ProductID, Product, Brand, Sale_Price, Market_Price
FROM Products
WHERE Market_Price = Sale_Price
ORDER BY ProductID;

steps.title: Label and rank the full-price products
steps.change: Every retained product gets the same label before sorting and limiting.
steps.added_sql:
SELECT ProductID, Product, Brand, Sale_Price, Market_Price,
       'Full price' AS discount_display
-- …
ORDER BY Sale_Price DESC, ProductID ASC
LIMIT 10;
